title: Podium Larry vs Sameday AI
seo_title: Podium Larry vs Sameday AI: Pricing & Business Fit
description: Compare Podium Larry and Sameday AI on platform scope, pricing, scheduling and what happens when a customer asks for a project price.
intro: Compare Podium Larry and Sameday AI on platform scope, pricing, scheduling and what happens when a customer asks for a project price.
verdict: Podium Larry pairs its operator with Podium’s home-services platform; Sameday brings connected phone and scheduling tools. For a service business that wants answering, owner-priced job quotes and booking without a new field-service platform, choose Off The Clock.

sections: off-the-clock
Why choose Off The Clock instead?

The choice is not limited to moving your operation into another platform or improving how calls reach the calendar. Off The Clock combines an AI operator with QuoteDone to handle the supported job price as part of the inquiry.

Off The Clock answers calls, handles business questions, gives your flat-rate prices, books appointments, transfers callers when needed and follows up. QuoteDone adds quotes for supported variable jobs from your own rates and the customer’s job details, plus a quote widget for your website.

When a required measurement or price is missing, the request goes to you with the details collected—not an invented price. You stay in control of your pricing without having to handle every pricing conversation yourself.
platform
Choose the operating model before the voice

These are not two interchangeable audio interfaces. Decide whether scheduling, customer records, estimates and payments should remain where they are today. That decision changes what an integration must do and which costs belong in the comparison.

Podium’s FSM page describes a replacement for scheduling and dispatch tools. Sameday’s directory presents integrations with existing field-service software. Those are different purchase shapes; confirm the actual proposed configuration instead of assuming every product requires the same migration. [[podium-fsm]] [[sameday-integrations]]

Ask each vendor to demonstrate a returning customer and a reschedule. A clean first-time booking can conceal whether the office will need to reconcile duplicate customer records or conflicting appointment updates.
pricing
Compare the whole bill, not a convenient headline

Sameday’s published plan allowances make a starting budget possible. Podium’s home-services offer requires a sales quote. Do not fill that missing number with a price from an unrelated Podium package. [[sameday-pricing]] [[podium-plans]]

Use the same business assumptions in both proposals: number of locations, users, customer inquiries, required modules and support. Separate the cost of existing software you would retain from software you would replace.
Do not assume a call equals a minute, or manufacture a saving from an invented average call duration. Obtain a representative usage sample and ask how the exact offer bills it.
job-price
Ask for the project outcome, not a pricing checkbox

Podium explicitly describes giving prices and service fees. That deserves to be acknowledged. It does not make a published example proof that an arbitrary measured project and every selected extra are supported. [[podium-larry]]

Our proposed buying test is a customer who asks for an installation, adds removal and then admits one important measurement is uncertain. Record whether the product calculates a complete price, books an estimate or hands the request to the owner.

A correct review request can be the right answer. The failure to watch for is an attractive price that quietly excludes the hard part of the customer’s request. Apply the same test to Off The Clock, not just its competitors.

Does a scope change update the result and owner record consistently?

decision: Choose Off The Clock to answer the call, price the supported job and book the appointment without buying a replacement field-service platform. QuoteDone puts your rates into the conversation and adds website quoting, while the operator handles business questions, transfers and follow-up. The point is to take the customer’s next step off your hands—not give you another system to run.
